ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two ideal operational amplifiers in the figure. The non-inverting input terminal of the left op-amp is connected to +1 V through a 1 kΩ resistor; because no current is drawn by the input terminals of an ideal op-amp, the voltage of this non-inverting terminal is +1 V. The inverting input node of the left op-amp is connected to -2 V through 1 kΩ, and is connected to the output node of the left op-amp through another 1 kΩ resistor; denote this output as V1. V1 is also directly connected to the non-inverting input terminal of the right op-amp. The right op-amp is a non-inverting amplification structure: the inverting input terminal is connected at the voltage-dividing point of two 1 kΩ resistors, one 1 kΩ connected to Vout, and the other 1 kΩ connected to ground. Reasoning: For an ideal op-amp with negative feedback, the voltage of the inverting input terminal of the left op-amp equals the voltage of the non-inverting input terminal, so the voltage of the left inverting node is +1 V. Write KCL for this inverting node: the algebraic sum of the currents flowing to the -2 V branch and to the V1 branch is 0, namely (1 - (-2))/1k + (1 - V1)/1k = 0. Simplifying gives 3 + 1 - V1 = 0, so V1 = 4 V. This V1 is applied to the non-inverting input terminal of the right op-amp, therefore the non-inverting input terminal of the right op-amp is 4 V. Negative feedback makes the inverting input terminal of the right op-amp also 4 V. The right inverting input terminal is the midpoint of two equal 1 kΩ resistors between Vout and ground, so its voltage is Vout/2. Thus Vout/2 = 4, obtaining Vout = 8 V.

method.method_draft: First determine the left op-amp output. Since the ideal non-inverting input draws no current, its voltage is +1 V, so feedback forces the left inverting node to +1 V. Apply KCL at that node: (1−(−2))/1k + (1−V1)/1k = 0, giving V1=4 V. This V1 is applied to the non-inverting input of the second op-amp. Negative feedback forces the second inverting input to 4 V. The two equal 1 kΩ resistors from Vout to ground make the inverting-node voltage Vout/2, so Vout/2=4 and Vout=8 V.
